newsitem.title: USA: NYS Assembly approves its bill to cut sales taxes.
newsitem.headline: NYS Assembly approves its bill to cut sales taxes.

text.p: The New York State Assembly on Wednesday said it approved its bill to phase-out the state's four-percent clothing sales tax starting March 1, 1998, too slow a schedule to suit the Gov George Pataki.

Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, pointed to a highly popular one-week moratorium in January 1997 on clothing sales taxes for items that cost less than $500, which was matched by most localities.

"New Yorkers want this policy continued and the real savings it provides to middle-class families squeezed by the need to make ends meet and the budget the Assembly has passed meets that demand," Silver said. His bill, which would let cities and towns also end their clothing sales taxes, first was approved by the Assembly in March 1995.
But the Republican governor has said he preferred a plan put forward by the Senate, which would begin this year.
